meta.title: The Red Rooster Academy — Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu in Charleroi
meta.description: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Grappling and Wrestling academy in Pironchamps (Charleroi). Method of Grandmaster Flavio Behring. For adults and kids from age 5.

hero.headline: The gentle art, taught with rigor and camaraderie.
hero.sub: From Hélio Gracie to Flavio Behring, all the way to the mats of Pironchamps — one lineage, one method, one family.

about.lead: The Red Rooster Academy is a Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu training team based in the Charleroi region, following the method of Grandmaster Flavio Behring.
about.body: Training here is serious, disciplined and welcoming, and fully in line with the principles of our Grandmaster Flavio Behring, a direct student of Hélio Gracie.

bjj-adults.title: Adults BJJ
bjj-adults.description: Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu in the Gi: technique, self-defense and sparring, for all levels.

bjj-kids.title: Kids BJJ
bjj-kids.description: From age 5: coordination, confidence, discipline and self-defense, in a fun, supportive setting.

grappling.title: No-Gi Grappling

schedule.note: First trial class is free — just show up 10 minutes before it starts.

fitness.question: Do I need to be fit to start?
fitness.answer: You don't need to be in peak shape to start training. In fact, BJJ is a great way to get fit. Everyone is welcome on the mats at the academy, whatever their fitness level.

experience.question: Do I need prior martial arts experience?
experience.answer: Not at all. If you've trained in another martial art before, that's a bonus, but no prior experience is required. Whether you're just starting your BJJ journey or you're a seasoned veteran, you'll always be welcome.

age.question: Am I too old?
age.answer: There's no such thing. It's never too late to start training BJJ. Our programs are designed for everyone. All students are encouraged to train within their own limits and push as hard as they want.

women.question: Do you have classes just for women?
women.answer: On request, we run self-defense workshops for women. This class suits women (age 13+) of any fitness level and is designed to introduce practical, basic self-defense skills.

kids-age.question: At what age can kids start Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu?
kids-age.answer: Every child is different. That said, we find around age 5 is a good time to start a martial art like BJJ. Our kids' program covers ages 5-14 and aims to make self-defense and physical education fun. We use conditioning and skill-based games to engage and challenge the kids. The benefits go well beyond the physical: courtesy, confidence, focus, discipline, teamwork, mental strength and self-control.

strength.question: Do I need to be strong to practice Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu?
strength.answer: The beauty of BJJ lies in its core principle: a smaller, weaker person can overcome a stronger, heavier opponent through leverage and technique.

bring.question: What should I bring?
bring.answer: All you need for your first class is comfortable clothing. A fitted t-shirt or rashguard works great, and shorts without pockets are best. For women, leggings and a top are perfect. If you already have a Jiu-Jitsu kimono, or "Gi," feel free to wear it. A water bottle and a small towel are also a good idea.

protection.question: Do I need protective gear?
protection.answer: Some students choose to wear a mouthguard when rolling, but that's entirely up to you.

other-academies.question: Do you welcome students from other academies?
other-academies.answer: We focus on community, not competition. Everyone is welcome.

patches.question: I have a Gi with patches from another club. Is that a problem?
patches.answer: No, that's not a problem at all.
